request: can you make a tiny do not disturb switch? just a heading, a line saying whether notifications are muted, and one button to mute or unmute, and it should remember the setting on the server so it's still there when i reload
design_rationale: A single switch should be calm and centred so the status line is the first thing you see: neutral base, one card, one full-width button.

verify.steps: Open the page and see Notifications are on, click Mute and see Notifications are muted, reload and still see muted, click Unmute and see Notifications are on.

why.services/mute.jac: MuteFlag node with the muted bool; read_mute (a walker that creates the flag under root on first visit and reports it) and flip_mute (a walker that flips the value and reports the flag).
why.components/QuietPanel.jac: The whole screen: the Do not disturb heading, the status line, the Mute/Unmute button, loading and error text.
why.main.jac: Registers the mute walkers, loads global.css and renders the panel.

write_reasoning.services/mute.jac: Endpoints are walkers in services/ that visit the flag node under root, so the client spawns them and reads .reports. read_mute creates the node only when root has none.
write_reasoning.components/QuietPanel.jac: The panel spawns read_mute in async can with entry and awaits flip_mute in an async handler, setting state from the reported node instead of reading again.
write_reasoning.main.jac: main.jac imports the walkers from services.mute with no leading dot so they are registered on the server, and returns the panel; one screen needs no router.

plan_call_reasoning: Plan the build: one screen with one saved on/off value, so a single panel component and a small walker server.
plan_reasoning: One screen: a Do not disturb heading, a status line and a Mute/Unmute button. The value lives in one node under root; a walker reads it (creating it on first visit) and another flips it and reports it. main.jac last.
plan_summary: Build plan written to .jaccoder/build_plan.json: a single-screen mute switch, 3 files leaf-first, the value on the server behind two walkers, nova/neutral/amber/inter.
journal:
# Agent journal

## Issues
- Endpoints are walkers so they must live in services/ and be named in main.jac's import, or root spawn gives 405.

## Learnings
- read_mute creates the MuteFlag node only when root has none, so the first visit shows Notifications are on.
- flip_mute reports the updated node, so the panel sets the state from result.reports[0] without a second read.
- The status line and the button text are render locals that follow the muted bool.

## Last Action
Built Do not disturb: a centred card with the status line and a Mute/Unmute button backed by two walkers. The preview shows Notifications are on, Mute gives Notifications are muted, and the setting survives a reload.
final:
Do not disturb is running: the card shows whether notifications are on or muted and the button flips the setting on the server. I muted, reloaded and still saw Notifications are muted, then unmuted and saw Notifications are on.

**Next steps**
- Add a quiet-hours schedule
- Mute per app
- Show when the setting last changed
